ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a regular hexagonal sheet of paper, with O marked near the center, and a small black dot indicating the center position. The three marked vertices of the hexagon are located in positions separated by one vertex: the upper-left vertex, the right-side vertex, and the lower-left vertex. Reasoning: Each marked vertex is to be folded to the center O. The crease must be the perpendicular bisector of the line segment connecting that vertex and O. For a regular hexagon, the distance from the center to a vertex equals the side length, so each such perpendicular bisector will pass through the two unmarked vertices adjacent to that folded vertex. The three creases corresponding to the three marked vertices exactly connect three unmarked alternating vertices, forming a triangle composed of three alternating vertices. The triangle formed by connecting alternating vertices of a regular hexagon is an equilateral triangle.

raw_record.question_text: A piece of paper in the shape of a regular hexagon, as shown, is folded so that the three marked vertices meet at the centre $O$ of the hexagon. What is the shape of the figure that is formed?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the paper is a regular hexagon with three marked vertices at alternate positions—upper-left, rightmost, and lower-left—and the center labeled O. From the text, each marked vertex is folded onto O. For each such fold, use the rule that the crease is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the original vertex to its image at O. In a regular hexagon, the center-to-vertex distance equals the side length, so the perpendicular bisector for each marked vertex passes through the two neighboring unmarked vertices. Thus the three fold creases connect the three unmarked alternate vertices, forming the central outline. Those three unmarked alternate vertices of a regular hexagon form an equilateral triangle, so the folded figure is an equilateral triangle.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一张正六边形纸片，中心附近标有 O，并有一个小黑点表示中心位置。六边形的三个被标记的顶点位于相隔一个顶点的位置：左上顶点、右侧顶点和左下顶点。推理：每个被标记的顶点都要折到中心 O。折痕必定是该顶点与 O 连线的垂直平分线。对于正六边形，中心到顶点的距离等于边长，所以每条这样的垂直平分线会经过该被折顶点相邻的两个未标记顶点。三个被标记顶点对应的三条折痕正好连接三个未标记的交替顶点，形成一个由三个交替顶点构成的三角形。正六边形的交替顶点连成的三角形是等边三角形。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct geometric crease-line route: determine each fold line as a perpendicular bisector, then identify the resulting boundary as the triangle joining the unmarked alternate vertices.
planner_metadata.image_role: The image supplies the arrangement of the regular hexagon, the location of O, and that the marked vertices are alternating vertices: upper-left, rightmost, and lower-left.
planner_metadata.text_role: The text specifies the folding action: the three marked vertices are folded to the center O, and asks for the resulting shape.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the folding fact that a crease is the perpendicular bisector between a point and its folded image, plus regular-hexagon facts: all vertices are equally spaced around the center, the center-to-vertex radius equals the side length, and alternate vertices form an equilateral triangle.
